derived_chemistry.comment: Both precursors survive, so the 900 C reaction MgO + WO3 -> MgWO4 is incomplete.  The leftover MgO greatly exceeds the leftover WO3 on a molar basis, implying an Mg-rich (Mg:W ~ 1.3) starting mixture and/or under-correction of the MgO amount (see notes).

notes: The 9.90-12.50 deg region was excluded from the refinement: it contains only the steeply rising direct-beam/air-scatter tail and no Bragg peaks.

All three phases require the same systematic peak shift of about +0.33 deg at 15-30 deg 2theta; without it every refined cell comes out ~1% too small.  It is modelled as a specimen displacement (-544 um, cos-theta dependence) rather than as a constant zero error, because that fits better (Rwp 7.99 vs 8.05%) and reproduces a(MgO) = 4.2122 A against the periclase value 4.2117 A (zero-error model: 4.2160 A).  The unreacted MgO thus acts as an internal standard.  Weight fractions are unchanged by this choice.

Observed intensities fall off systematically at low 2theta relative to any structural model.  This was absorbed with the GSAS-II Suortti surface-roughness function; the refined A lies outside the physical 0-1 range, so it is used as an empirical low-angle intensity correction (beam overflow / surface roughness) rather than as a measured roughness.  Weight fractions change by <1 abs% whether it is included or not.

No Brindley microabsorption correction was applied (particle sizes unknown).  MgO (mu ~ 100 /cm) is a much weaker absorber than MgWO4/WO3 (mu ~ 830-990 /cm), so the MgO weight fraction is more likely under- than over-estimated.
Atomic displacement parameters were held at the published single-crystal values; they cannot be refined meaningfully alongside the empirical low-angle correction.

WO3 oxygen positions were held at the Loopstra & Boldrup values; releasing them gave no improvement in Rwp (8.513 vs 8.516 in the equivalent test refinement) while moving some O atoms by >0.1 fractional units, i.e. overfitting.

Alternative WO3 polymorphs were tested with the identical protocol and rejected: orthorhombic beta-WO3 (Pnma) Rwp = 10.99%, triclinic delta-WO3 (P-1) worse than monoclinic at the matched stage with alpha, gamma within 0.17 deg of 90 deg.
Removing MgO from the model raises Rwp from 7.99% to 9.36% and leaves the 43.21 deg peak unfitted; removing WO3 raises it to 19.07%.

phases.structure_source: COD 2311041 (Loopstra & Boldrup, Acta Cryst. 1966), transformed to the P2_1/n setting

weight_fraction_basis: normalised over the three modelled crystalline phases (sums to 1)
